scope: Actual source-derived photo preparation in a standalone arm64 iOS 27.1 Simulator process; procedural fixtures, no app UI, camera, Photos picker, model or production data.

changes: Normalize the finite CI extent origin to zero before existing scaling and bounded rendering.
Move the existing finite/positive UIImage scale guard before the CI/CG branch.
source.extraction: The driver extracts the current enum byte-identically; only standalone imports are prefixed outside it. No production implementation copy is committed in the test.

reproduction.matrix: Four origins, all eight UIImage orientation values, scales 1/2, procedural asymmetric bitmap and 768-pixel maximum.
reproduction.cause: Original nil results coincided with scaled integral bounds of 769 by 513 for negative fractional origins, consistent with render-bound expansion. The retained probe does not distinguish render failure from rejection by the 768-pixel guard. Origin normalization restored bounded results.
reproduction.malformedScale: Public UIImage CI constructors retained NaN/infinite scales; the original CI branch returned images carrying those scales. The CG branch rejected them. Zero/negative requested scales normalized to 1 on this runtime.

memory.interpretation: Peak RSS includes fixture, runtime, decoder/backing realization and render transients. CIContext-created CGImage fixtures were not proven eager; their raw materialized mode labels must not be interpreted as an eager-decode control. Even the explicitly filled CGContext control peaked higher during preparation, so fixture allocation alone does not explain the peak. Internal costs remain unisolated; no memory optimization is established.

officialReferences.context: Apple documents render-region integralization/intersection and nil for empty or oversized extents.
This option controls intermediate caching; disabling it is not a guarantee of bounded peak decoding/render memory.

limits: Four orientation-aware drawn-reference corner samples and aspect/metadata checks are not full pixel equivalence or off-center marker coverage.
Malformed UIImage API handling is reproduced; no evidence that the real camera or picker supplies NaN/infinite scales.
Procedural Simulator observations do not validate physical device behavior, real camera/HEIC/JPEG decoding, full app UI, network isolation, meal recognition or nutrition accuracy.
